c11_eng_h_cbse_02_009: Bad luck isn't irony — the fearless title worn by frightened adults is. Check: expectation vs outcome?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_010: Don't grab the first dictionary sense — gather the sentence's clues; 'honing' implies years of practice. Check: what evidence clusters?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_011: In 'flagship' the ship is a vessel, not a state — same spelling, different morpheme. Check: suffix or compound?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_012: Inference isn't free opinion — anchor each claim to a textual clue. Check: which line proves it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_013: Don't hunt secret meanings — a claim needs recurring textual patterns behind it. Check: what's the anchor?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_014: A diary entry isn't a plot recap — it needs the persona's voice and textual detail. Check: whose voice is it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_015: Discussion isn't waiting to speak — it's building or challenging with evidence. Check: did you cite the text?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_001: Context is the chain — the 1922 dig caused the damage the 2005 scan had to dodge. Check: what caused what?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_002: The flashbacks aren't side-info — they build why the death stayed mysterious. Check: what do they explain?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_003: Atmosphere isn't an adjective — 'ghostly dust devils' and whispers build it. Check: which details create it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_004: Tut isn't a character with traits — he's rebuilt from evidence; the trail is the protagonist. Check: revealed or reconstructed?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_005: Akhenaten is a character here too — built from the author's chosen details. Check: how is Carter used?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_006: The mystery is the vehicle — how we investigate, and at what cost, is the theme. Check: subject or method?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_007: 'Gold' is a motif — the theme is the belief it carries about the afterlife. Check: object or idea?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_008: 'Like slices of bread' is a simile — and listen for the scanner's 'whir' too. Check: like or as present?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_009: A broken scanner isn't bad luck — the tomb's own sand defeating the probe is irony. Check: what reversed?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_010: 'Scudded' isn't just 'moved fast' — it means low clouds racing before wind. Check: what does the field suggest?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_011: 'Tomography' means slice-writing — morphology explains the word, register explains the choice. Check: why 'CT' later?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_012: An inference needs textual proof — 'the curse is real' has none. Check: which detail backs it?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_013: Critical doesn't mean complaining — analyse how the text builds meaning. Check: fault or framework?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_014: A report isn't a chronology — pick the angle the format wants. Check: what's the news angle?
c11_eng_h_cbse_03_015: Discussion needs evidence-backed stances, not louder opinions. Check: what's your citation?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_001: Chinese painters knew perspective — they chose conceptual completeness over optical illusion. Check: couldn't or wouldn't?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_002: In an essay the thesis is the hero — the clash of evidence is the conflict. Check: what's the claim?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_003: The real setting is two worldviews — China and Flanders are just doorways. Check: place or philosophy?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_004: A trait is proven by a costly choice — not an adjective with a quote. Check: what did it cost them?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_005: Each name is a move — ask why this authority backs this claim. Check: why an economist on forests?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_006: The essay isn't a contest — it's two different goals; shanshui is cosmology, not landscape. Check: better or different?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_007: The anecdotes carry the theme — Shanshui is Yin-Yang-Middle Void, not a technique. Check: story or idea?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_008: 'Sustainable development' is a term, not a metaphor — check for the A-is-B transfer. Check: literal or figurative?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_009: Magic isn't irony — look for expectation colliding with outcome. Check: what's the contradiction?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_010: Clues can hide across paragraphs — and 'gripped the imagination' isn't a hand. Check: literal or figurative?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_011: 'Prima facie' isn't fancy talk — it carries a fixed legal meaning. Check: would plain English lose precision?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_012: Cite two details and the link between them — 'I think' isn't enough. Check: where's your evidence?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_013: Understand the argument's own logic before judging it — analysis precedes evaluation. Check: inside or outside the text?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_014: A list of facts isn't an argument — build a point-evidence-explanation chain. Check: where's the link?
c11_eng_h_cbse_04_015: Discussion means answering the last speaker — not reading your prepared note. Check: did you engage their point?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_001: The Green Movement isn't the Green Revolution — one critiques the other's ecological cost. Check: which 'green'?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_002: Gaitonde didn't time-travel — he saw a present where Panipat went differently. Check: past or parallel?
c11_eng_h_cbse_05_003: The settings aren't just places — each reveals a layer of the alternate history. Check: how does the mood shift?
